title: Azure AD Integration
description: Set up Azure Active Directory authentication for ASP.NET Core applications using OpenID Connect and MSAL.

data.text: **Azure Active Directory (Azure AD)**, now part of Microsoft Entra ID, is Microsoft's cloud-based identity and access management service. It is the most common enterprise identity provider for organizations using Microsoft 365, Office 365, and Azure cloud services. Integrating with Azure AD enables your ASP.NET Core application to leverage enterprise-grade authentication, conditional access, and MFA without building them yourself.

data.title: Enterprise Benefits
items: Pre-integrated with millions of enterprise user accounts
Supports conditional access policies (location, device, risk)
SCIM provisioning for automatic user lifecycle management
Comprehensive audit logs and security reporting
B2B and B2C scenarios supported in the same tenant

data.title: Use Microsoft.Identity.Web
data.text: The Microsoft.Identity.Web library simplifies Azure AD integration in ASP.NET Core. It handles token acquisition, cache serialization, and downstream API calls with minimal configuration.

data.title: Registration Steps
items: Navigate to Azure AD > App Registrations > New Registration.
Name your application and select supported account types.
Set the redirect URI to https://localhost:5001/signin-oidc for development.
Note the Application (client) ID and Directory (tenant) ID.
Under Certificates & Secrets, create a client secret or upload a certificate.
Under API Permissions, add Microsoft Graph permissions (e.g., User.Read).
Grant admin consent if required for your application.

data.caption: Azure AD OpenID Connect flow for an ASP.NET Core web application.
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant App as ASP.NET Core App
    participant Azure as Azure AD
    U->>App: Access protected page
    App->>U: 302 Redirect to Azure AD authorize endpoint
    U->>Azure: Authenticate (credentials + MFA)
    Azure->>U: 302 Redirect back with auth code
    U->>App: Callback with authorization code
    App->>Azure: POST token endpoint (code + client secret)
    Azure->>App: Return ID token, access token, refresh token
    App->>App: Validate tokens, create auth cookie
    App->>U: Serve protected content

data.text: Practical Implementation: ASP.NET Core with Microsoft.Identity.Web

data.title: Program.cs — Azure AD OpenID Connect
data.content: Configure Azure AD authentication using the Microsoft.Identity.Web library.

data.title: appsettings.json — Azure AD Settings
data.content: Store Azure AD configuration in appsettings.json.

data.title: Accessing downstream APIs with acquired tokens
data.content: Use TokenAcquisition to get tokens for Microsoft Graph or other protected APIs.

data.title: Token Cache in Production
data.text: In production, use a distributed token cache (e.g., Redis or SQL) instead of in-memory caching. In-memory caches do not work across multiple server instances and are lost on app restart.

Azure AD Conditional Access policies allow administrators to enforce access rules based on user location, device compliance, risk level, and application sensitivity. When a policy blocks access, Azure AD returns specific error codes and descriptions in the authentication response. Your application should gracefully handle these scenarios — for example, displaying a message that the user must enroll a compliant device rather than showing a generic error.

data.title: Do Not Build Your Own MFA
data.text: If Azure AD is your IdP, always use its built-in MFA and Conditional Access. Building custom MFA logic in your application defeats the purpose of centralizing authentication and often creates security gaps.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Azure AD (Microsoft Entra ID) is the standard enterprise IdP for Microsoft shops
Register your app in the Azure Portal to get client ID and tenant ID
Microsoft.Identity.Web simplifies token acquisition and cache management
Use distributed token caches in production for scalability
Leverage Conditional Access instead of building custom MFA logic
data.takeaway: Azure AD integration turns your ASP.NET Core app into an enterprise-ready application with minimal custom authentication code.
